findings.title: AIM raises StrongREJECT harmfulness by +0.18 on Qwen2.5-0.5B; on Qwen3-0.6B it works only with thinking enabled
findings.summary: On the 313 StrongREJECT prompts, the AIM role-play jailbreak raised the mean StrongREJECT score of Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct from 0.153 to 0.335 (paired diff +0.182, 95% CI 0.140-0.223). That clears the hypothesised +0.15 as a point estimate but not significantly (one-sided p = 0.07). On Qwen3-0.6B with thinking disabled (the primary condition), AIM did not help (0.354 -> 0.309, diff -0.045, CI -0.093 to 0.003). 34% of its AIM outputs degenerated into repeated "AIM:" lines with no content, a capability failure rather than a refusal. With thinking enabled, the same attack raised Qwen3-0.6B to 0.568

findings.title: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct refuses 40% of XSTest safe prompts while refusing 84.5% of the unsafe contrasts
findings.summary: Under direct prompting (greedy, no system prompt) Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct fully or partially refused 100 of 250 XSTest-v2 safe prompts (40.0%, 95% CI 34.1-46.2%), four times the 10% threshold in the hypothesis and well above GPT-4's 8.4% in the XSTest paper. The XSTest string-match classifier, which agrees well with human labels on this model (kappa 0.79 on our hand-labelled subset), gives 48.8%. On the 200 unsafe contrast prompts it refused 84.5% (78.8-88.9%). So it separates safe from unsafe only weakly. Over-refusal is concentrated in historical_events (76%), privacy_fictional (68%) and safe_

findings.title: Qwen3-0.6B gives more harmful direct-request compliance than Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (StrongREJECT 0.354 vs 0.153)
findings.summary: With no jailbreak, Qwen3-0.6B (non-thinking) scored 0.354 on StrongREJECT against 0.153 for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (paired diff +0.201, 95% CI 0.159-0.243, n = 313 identical prompts). It also refused fewer XSTest unsafe prompts (62.5% vs 84.5%; paired diff -0.22, McNemar p = 5e-9). Enabling thinking raised Qwen3's direct StrongREJECT score further to 0.435 (+0.081, CI 0.044-0.119). The newer, slightly larger release trades over-refusal (15.6% vs 40% on XSTest safe) for markedly more harmful compliance. This matches the direction of the SLM jailbreak paper (direct ASR 0.36 vs 0.13).
